briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Rescheduling Momentum Builds Nationally While Michigan Operators Find Cracks of Light in the Tax Fight
briefs.top: Federal cannabis reform hit a real inflection point this week as DEA lawyers filed final briefs telling a judge marijuana no longer belongs in Schedule I, while Compass Pathways' psilocybin therapy edges toward a historic FDA approval. Back home, Michigan operators are watching a repeal bill and a favorable Supreme Court search ruling chip away at the 24% wholesale tax's damage, even as new stores keep opening across the state.

local.text: The Michigan Supreme Court barred warrantless vehicle searches based on the smell of marijuana alone and struck down blanket probation marijuana bans, giving operators and consumers a real legal shield against overreach.

State Rep. filed HB 6224 on July 29 to repeal the 24% wholesale marijuana tax entirely, which would leave the voter-approved 10% retail excise and 6% sales tax intact — the second bill this year aiming to kill the levy after Sen. Jonathan Lindsey's bipartisan-backed SB 810.

Common Citizen is set to open a new Eastpointe dispensary after reaching a court-approved deal giving it until Dec. 1 to finish buildout — proof new retail is still landing even in a brutal margin environment.

A decade-old Michigan pharmacy law signed by former Gov. Rick Snyder could be triggered by federal marijuana rescheduling, potentially opening a brand-new licensing lane that would let weed be sold at pharmacies like CVS or Walgreens.

Recreational sales fell to $1.48 billion in the first half of 2026 as the wholesale tax bit into margins, but Treasury is offering penalty and interest relief for businesses making good-faith quarterly payments during this transition year — a real cushion while the repeal push and appeal play out.

national.text: DEA lawyers filed their final post-hearing brief on Aug. 25 arguing marijuana can no longer remain in Schedule I, citing HHS and FDA research on accepted medical uses for pain, nausea and anorexia — a strong signal ahead of the judge's recommendation.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin therapy COMP360 is riding a 3-for-3 Phase 3 record, an FDA rolling NDA review, and a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher that could compress review to just 1-2 months — with analysts eyeing a year-end 2026 approval as the first classic psychedelic ever cleared by the FDA.

Curaleaf formally launched its hostile takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis on Aug. 18, offering $4/share in cash-and-stock to build what it calls the preeminent global cannabis platform with deep exposure to U.S. regulatory tailwinds; the tender stays open into December.

The bipartisan SAFE Banking Act picked up two more House cosponsors in late August, keeping banking-access reform alive as one of the more viable near-term wins working through Congress alongside rescheduling.

New FBI data show more than 200,000 marijuana arrests last year, with 92% stemming from simple possession — the kind of enforcement math that's fueling the Cato Institute's push and giving rescheduling advocates fresh ammunition heading into the judge's recommendation.
